header:
Date: 2026-11-25 | Start: 15:00 UTC | Duration: 55m
Redwood: Jordan Lee (AE), Maya Patel (SE), Carlos Nguyen (SE)
Celestia Payments: Aisha Khan (Head of ML), Tom Reyes (CTO), Lena Ortiz (DevOps), Rahul Sen (Product)
summary: Redwood AE/SE walked Celestia Payments through the Redwood Console focused on usage analytics, per-route dashboards, and cost breakdown. Customer is evaluating hosted vs dedicated for a payments fraud scoring use case. Key concerns: latency SLOs, data residency, VPC peering, and predictable unit cost for high-volume scoring. Next steps: pricing + dedicated options, share runbook and sample traffic, schedule POC scoping.
transcript:
00:00 Jordan: hey everyone thanks for joining, i'm Jordan from Redwood, uh we'll do a quick intro and then Maya will jump into the console walkthrough.
00:08 Aisha: hey thanks, excited to see the usage analytics piece, we've been trying to get a per-route cost view for our fraud model.
00:15 Jordan: perfect, thats the goal. quick intros?
00:20 Tom: Tom Reyes, CTO - i'll focus on infra questions.
00:23 Lena: Lena, DevOps, i'll ask about networking and VPC.
00:26 Jordan: great, Maya over to you.
00:30 Maya: ok i'm pulling up the console now, can everyone see my screen?
00:34 Aisha: yep, looks good.
00:37 Maya: starting on the home overview - usage tab shows tokens, requests, lat p50/p95, and cost by model. we auto-aggregate by route so you can see per-endpoint breakdowns for your fraud-scorer route vs chat endpoints.
00:52 Rahul: is that per-token cost calc using our model mix? how do we handle different quantized variants?
00:58 Maya: good q. the cost calc pulls model profile you select, we show effective per-token cost with quantization adjustments. note sometimes the auto-rename of models in the console is a little fuzzy - you might see 'redwood-gpt-0' in the demo account.
01:12 Aisha: got it. can we filter by customer segment and production vs staging?
01:17 Maya: yes, there's a route tag filter - you can tag routes as prod/stage, and we overlay traffic split and cost. i'll jump to the per-route dashboard now.
01:26 Maya: per-route dashboard has tokens, latency heatmap, throughput, and a cost waterfall showing model compute, GPU minute allocation, and caching savings. here's an example for the fraud-scorer route.
01:40 Tom: that cost waterfall - is the GPU minute allocation an observed metric or a projected allocation?
01:45 Maya: observed. we infer GPU time from serving logs and the runtime's kernel profiling. caveat: for Dedicated pools we give an allocation estimate vs hosted where it's fully usage-based.
01:58 Lena: speaking of Dedicated, how does VPC peering or private deployment change the billing? any egress fees?
02:05 Jordan: short answer: Dedicated and Private have different billing constructs. Dedicated is commit/flat with unit overage; Private has a platform fee plus support - egress still follows your cloud provider policies. we'll send a detailed sheet.
02:18 Aisha: our big ask is predictable unit cost - we scale to 10s of millions of requests during peak. how do we prevent cost surprise?
02:25 Maya: two levers: per-route quotas + automatic caching. For fraud-scorer we recommend prefix KV caching for common transactions. Also you can pin a model variant to a cheaper quantized profile with a small drop in quality and we surface the expected quality delta.
02:42 Rahul: quality delta metric - is it automated A/B or do we need manual evals?
02:47 Maya: we integrate with Redwood Optimize where we run evals on your prompt sets and show regression alerts. you can do canary rollouts across model variants.
02:55 Tom: latency targets? we need sub-60ms p95 for scoring.
02:59 Maya: runtime supports continuous batching and KV-cache; with pinned smaller context sizes and optimized kernels we can hit sub-60ms for many architectures but it depends on model/seq length. we'll need sample payloads to confirm.
03:13 Jordan: maybe i can highlight the per-route alerting - you can set cost thresholds by route and get Slack/email alerts, also automated fallback to cheaper model if cost grows unexpectedly.
03:26 Aisha: nice. how accurate are the cost forecasts? we run internal e2e billing reconciliation monthly.
03:33 Carlos: our forecasts are within ~5-8% historically when traffic profile is stable; spikes due to sudden seq length or model change can deviate. we show a reconciliation export for finance teams.
03:46 Lena: on the private side, what's the onboarding for VPC peering? ccan we use our KMS?
03:52 Maya: yes, Private supports customer KMS/HSM for keys, and VPC peering plus private control plane. onboarding typically 4-6 weeks for air-gapped or on-prem variants.
04:05 Tom: regulatory - do you have SOC2 type 2 and ISO?
04:09 Jordan: yes we have SOC2 and ISO27001, also offer audit logs per request; will share the security pack.
04:16 Aisha: any references in payments or finance?
04:19 Jordan: we have a couple anonymized case studies and a compliance add-on used by fintech customers; i'll include them in the follow up.
04:26 Rahul: can you show a deep link from the dashboard to a trace? i want to see request-level KV hits.
04:31 Maya: yep clicking on a high-p95 spike, we see the trace, model variant used, KV-cache hit/miss ratio, and tokens per request. note transcriptions sometimes show 'K-V cash' in the auto notes - ignore that.
04:45 Aisha: there was mention of prefix caching - how do you manage cache invalidation for fraud rules?
04:50 Maya: cache TTLs are configurable per-route, and we surface cache hit rate; for fraud you can set shorter TTLs or use conditional invalidation via webhook.
04:59 Tom: procurement question - annual or monthly committed for Dedicated?
05:04 Jordan: Dedicated is usually annual with monthly invoicing options, discounts at capacity tiers. we'll put options in the pricing sheet.
05:12 Lena: question about tracing retention and PIIs in logs - do request payloads get stored?
05:18 Carlos: by default logs are scrubbed but you can opt into longer retention and encryption-at-rest with customer-managed keys; we also support token redaction.
05:29 Aisha: this is helpful - can we run a small POC that replicates our peak pattern with a smaller sample?
05:33 Jordan: absolutely. typical POC is 2-4 weeks, Redwood provides pilot credits for hosted or we can spin a Dedicated pilot for the trial period.
05:42 Rahul: for sizing the Dedicated pool, would you want QPS and average seq length per route?
05:47 Maya: exactly, QPS, p50/p95 seq length distribution, and concurrency targets; the sample CSV works well.
05:55 Tom: ok let's talk timelines - we want a POC before end of Q1 2027.
05:59 Jordan: sounds good, we'll aim for scoping call in early December.
06:03 Aisha: any gotchas on the console before we sign up?
06:06 Maya: just naming and model aliasing in sandbox, and sometimes the auto-grouping of ephemeral routes needs manual tags. nothing blocking.
06:14 Jordan: recap - Jordan to send pricing and case studies, Maya to share runbook + dashboard exports, Lena to confirm networking questions and provide egress policy, Aisha to share traffic CSV. schedule follow-up POC scoping.
06:30 Tom: thanks all.
06:33 Jordan: thanks everyone! we'll follow up with notes and links.
06:36 [call ends]
